definitions.explanation: Expressing that something is impressive, remarkable, or extraordinary. Very commonly used in casual conversation.
Originally meant something frightening or extreme (can still be used this way).

examples.japanese: すごい！{上手|じょうず}ですね。
examples.english: Amazing! You're so good at it.

examples.japanese: すごい{人|ひと}がたくさんいますね。
あの{映画|えいが}はすごかった。
{彼女|かのじょ}は{語学|ごがく}の{才能|さいのう}がすごくて、{五|ご}か{国語|こくご}も{話|はな}せるんだって。
examples.english: She has an incredible talent for languages—apparently she can speak five languages.

examples.japanese: {台風|たいふう}の{風|かぜ}がすごくて、{外|そと}に{出|で}られなかった。{木|き}も{何本|なんぼん}か{倒|たお}れたらしい。
examples.english: The typhoon winds were terrible, so we couldn't go outside. Apparently several trees fell over too.

notes: すごい conjugates as an i-adjective: すごくない (negative), すごくて (te-form), すごかった (past). The kanji {凄|すご}い can be used but hiragana is more common. In casual speech, すごく is often used as an intensifier meaning 'very' (e.g., すごくおいしい - very delicious). Young people often say すげー as a casual variant.
